decisions.reason: It is close to the firm's core heat-exchange know-how, and the firm's strong in-house R&D and research links make it likely to learn from early market use and improve rather than withdraw it.
As an incremental extension of the established condenser business in a growing market, it fits the firm's absorptive capacity well and is more likely to be refined than discontinued.

It is also close to the existing offer, but because it appears similar to another newly launched condenser product there is a somewhat higher chance of portfolio rationalization, though the firm would still most likely keep it.
This product builds directly on the firm's installed-base service and repair capabilities, so its relatedness to existing knowledge and customer relationships makes withdrawal unlikely.
A customized industrial air cooler line matches the firm's established solution-selling model, broad service support, and engineering strengths, which strongly favors continued commercialization.

These repair inserts extend the firm's lifecycle-service business and rely on highly related technical knowledge, so a capable German machinery firm with active R&D would usually keep and improve them.
